name: Salesrobot

mentions.evidence: ~$87.5k L30, ~$1.68M all-time, no active subscriptions shown (credits/usage), ~4,100 users claimed.

whyThisMatters:
It sends cold outreach on LinkedIn and on email. A campaign can be a connection note, an email, a video, a voice note. Drip sequences. It notices who replied. You pull a list from a LinkedIn search, from Sales Navigator, or from a CSV. Replies land in one inbox. There's analytics, and a team can sit in there together.

There's an API and webhooks, plus custom variables, so you're not stuck clicking around in their screens. The site talks to B2B sales teams and to agencies. Next to the paid product they've got playbooks, templates, and free tools. The free stuff helps you find leads. The paid stuff does the sending and holds the inbox.

They're also pushing something called Kuron. An AI inbox that takes a real reply, works through the objections, and tries to book a call in your voice. The campaign is the first message. Kuron, the way they describe it, is what happens after someone writes back.

People pay in credits, not seats. A subscriber count is the wrong shape. The credits get spent on lists, sequences, replies, and that shared inbox.

Video notes and voice notes at scale are the bit plain email tools skip. Pulling a list from Sales Navigator matters when the list already lives there. Nobody wants to retype it into a second box.
